key_insight: Physics-constrained causal discovery can identify constitutive mechanism dependencies from displacement fields, while correlated observational data can hide the correct attribution.
engineering_relevance: Climate-chamber interventions can help build constitutive models that generalize to unseen environments without measuring stresses or internal variables.
method: Embed balance laws and constitutive skeletons in time-unrolled causal models scored by weak-form equilibrium gaps.
Use adaptive lasso and a NOTEARS-type acyclicity constraint to select mechanism dependencies.
Compute a Gauss–Newton identifiability certificate via automatic differentiation to guide greedy D-optimal test design.
evidence_signal: On a synthetic plate with 8 true edges among 13 candidates, interventional data recovered the exact graph in 7/10 runs at 0.01-pixel displacement noise; prediction errors stayed within 3.2%, versus up to 41.5% for observationally discovered models in hot, humid climates.
watch_item: Evidence is synthetic, and noise bias in the weak-form score remains a primary limitation.
paper_title: Physics-constrained differentiable causal discovery of constitutive mechanisms through boundary value problems
